## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `59470e8d9a6d9b070d08c6137c8420e68aa5a780`
Local-runs: none

Scope: PR objectstack-ai/objectui#12312 for card #12301, judged on the card body and its three comments (triage 6138546687, claim 6139050988, os-dev-report 6139566902), the PR body, its 13-file list (+308/-30) and the net diff against `main`, and the head's check-runs. Published surfaces were measured from the source at the head (contents API) and, for the objectstack side, from the `e540e7ffb` checkout the PR body cites. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`@object-ui/i18n` published surface — WIDENS; declared right.** `packages/i18n/package.json` `exports` reaches `.`, `./locales` and `./locales/*`. `src/index.ts` re-exports `en` and `type TranslationKeys` from `./locales/en.js`, where `TranslationKeys = typeof en` over a pack that ends `as const`; `src/locales/index.ts` re-exports all ten packs. So every pack key is published, and the diff adds two to all ten packs, `oauth.consent.unidentified` and `oauth.consent.clientId`, inside the existing `oauth.consent` group: the `en` value and `TranslationKeys` each gain two members, nothing is removed or renamed (the dev report's `check:i18n-drift` reading, "2 key(s) added, 0 removed", agrees). Right: no existing `en` key says it (the base pack's only "identif" hit is `writeStrippedPrimaryKey`), both keys are read by the page, neither name carries a product word (ADR-0060 ratchet), and the nine translations say what `en` says.

2. **`@object-ui/console` published surface — UNCHANGED; right.** `apps/console/package.json` `exports` reaches `.` only (`plugin.js` / `plugin.d.ts`). The diff touches `src/pages/auth/OAuthConsentPage.tsx` and a new test, not `plugin.ts`; the SPA under `dist` is shipped bytes, not a published accept set.

3. **The page's accept set from the server — NARROWED to the served contract; right.** Before: a `data` envelope or a bare body, `name` or `client_name`, `icon` or `logo_uri`, and the raw `client_id` as the name of last resort. After: a bare body, a non-empty trimmed `client_name`, `logo_uri`, and the id never in the name's place. Measured against `@objectstack/client` at `e540e7ffb`: `OAuthApplicationPublic` is a `Pick` of `client_id`, `client_name`, `client_uri`, `logo_uri`, `contacts`, `tos_uri`, `policy_uri`, `redirect_uris`; `oauth.applications.getPublic` returns it unwrapped, and the client's CHANGELOG records the four bare better-auth OAuth routes as served with no envelope. Dropping `name`, `icon` and the envelope is the contract-first move (objectui Commandment 0.1: no alias chain in a consumer); keeping the id out of the name is the triage direction.

4. **The request — right.** `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth2/public-client?client_id=…` with `encodeURIComponent`, `credentials: 'include'` kept. The route is the ledger row `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth2/public-client` in `auth-route-ledger.ts` (`client: 'oauth.applications.getPublic'`, `requires: 'oidcProvider'`) and sits in `BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE`; the old path `/oauth2/applications/ID/public` appears nowhere in the ledger. The new test pins the page's URL to the one the real SDK builds, not to a copied string. No server change and no new route, as the card, the triage and the claim all require: the file list confirms.

5. **The session gate (`userId` in the lookup effect's deps) — accepted, harmless either way.** The ledger does not record which routes carry `sessionMiddleware`, and the PR body's reading of the vendor source is not re-measured here. If the route needs a session, the gate avoids a wasted 401; if it does not, the existing effect bounces a signed-out visitor to `/login` before any lookup. The signed-out pin (zero lookups) holds in both cases.

6. **The could-not-identify state — right by the triage pins.** A registered client shows its name and logo; a 404 `not_found`, any other non-2xx, a network failure and a 2xx without `client_name` each show the `role=alert` block with "Client ID" and the id exactly once, in a `code` node; in flight shows neither name nor id. `Alert`, `AlertTitle` and `AlertDescription` are published by `@object-ui/components` (`ui/index.ts` re-exports `./alert`, whose primitive carries `role="alert"`), so `findByRole('alert')` reads the real primitive.

7. **A first direct `@objectstack/client` import under `apps/console/src` — right, with one flag.** The page imports only the type `OAuthApplicationPublic` (erased at build); the test imports `ObjectStackClient` at runtime. The package is already a console devDependency, so nothing is added to the manifest. Flag: no other console source file imported it before this diff, and the declared range `^17.3.0` predates the type, which the client's CHANGELOG first exports at 17.4.0; the lockfile resolves 17.7.0, so the head builds and type-checks, but the declared floor is now stale. Not a FAIL (an app's devDependency, lockfile-pinned); carried to ③.

8. **Governed surfaces — none.** The file list is `.changeset/`, `apps/console/src/**` and `packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success on the head. Head repo equals base repo, 338 changed lines, still draft.

### ② Semver level

**Not consistent — this is the FAIL.** `.changeset/12301-consent-public-client-name.md` declares `'@object-ui/console': patch` and `'@object-ui/i18n': patch`, and its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the PR body's line is `Clause-②: yes`, matching the claim. The arm is right (① item 1: a published widening, and nothing narrows). The level is not: a `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor` (objectstack AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3, the rule that gives the `(widening)` arm its meaning), and this repository's landed changesets level this exact shape that way — `view.noObject`, `organization.settings.slugLockedNote`, `actions.notAvailableForRecord`, `console.studio.accessRequired` and `approvalsInbox.decisionPanelOffRequestPage` each landed as `'@object-ui/i18n': minor`; the two landed i18n-key widenings at `patch` rode an `'@object-ui/app-shell': minor` in the same changeset, so the fixed group still moved a minor. Here nothing in the changeset carries a `minor`, so a published widening would ship as a patch of the fixed group. (One 17.7.0 CHANGELOG entry did level a `Clause-②: yes` widening under Patch Changes; it is the exception the rule and the five precedents stand against.) No gate on the head judges this: `Changeset Declaration` is presence, `Changeset Bump Policy` is no-major, `Changeset Fixed Group Check` is workspace classification, `Changeset Claim Re-read` is report-only prose, and no objectui script reads the `Clause-②` arm against the bump — this record is the compensating control.

Remedy, one line in the patch round: `'@object-ui/i18n': minor`. `@object-ui/console` stays `patch` (its published entry is unchanged; the `console.studio.accessRequired` precedent splits the same way). Everything else in the changeset body — the route, the fields, the could-not-identify state, "no key is removed or changed", "no export, prop or type member moves" — reads true against the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the os-dev-report: none. Each dev deviation, answered:

- Citation by symbol and quoted text instead of file:line — accepted; objectui Commandment 11 bans a line address in a PR body, so this is the required form.
- Vendor source read from the `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.3` tarball — accepted as a read; the field mapping it supports is confirmed independently from `OAuthApplicationPublic` (① item 3); the session claim is not re-measured and is harmless either way (① item 5).
- Vitest run widened by `product-neutral-renderer.ratchet.test.ts` — accepted; it reads locale keys, so it belongs in the run.
- ESLint narrowed to the 12 changed files — accepted; the head's `Lint` check-run is success and carries the repo-wide verdict.
- Model-free commit trailers and the session-URL PR footer — accepted; that is objectui AGENTS.md's own rule.

Out-of-scope findings (carrier none), answered:

- `oauth.consent.unknownApp` opening the title in lower case — accepted as an acceptance note, with one escalation to the dispatching seat: this diff makes that title reachable on every consent render (in flight, and whenever the lookup gives no name), where before the raw id usually stood in. Whether a polish card is filed is the seat's call; not this PR's scope.
- The consent POST's redirect alias chain (`redirect_uri`, then `redirectURI`, then `url`) — escalated: untouched here and unmeasured, but it is the alias-chain shape Commandment 0.1 refuses in a consumer. The dispatching seat should measure the vendor's consent answer and file a card if the chain tolerates spellings the route never answers.

Reviewer flags:

- The `@objectstack/client` floor `^17.3.0` in `apps/console/package.json` is below 17.4.0, the first version exporting `OAuthApplicationPublic` (① item 7). Escalated; the patch round may raise it to `^17.4.0` in the same commit, but it is not a landing blocker on its own.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-13T06:31Z: 33 runs. 29 completed success, among them `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Repo Gates`, `Test` and all twelve `Test (shard k/12)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the four `Changeset …` checks, `label`, and `Live E2E (informational)`. 3 completed skipped (the two coverage jobs and `dependabot`). 1 still in progress: `Spec Main Shape Gate`. The gate conclusions are the check-runs' own; none was re-run here.

Reviewed-by: `session_01RZYixBnXPWvcm2YenWo6eJ`
